STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole pear on an empty white plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is square-ish, about 24 cm across, so its area is roughly 24 × 24 ≈ 550 cm² (a bit less because of the rounded corners). The pear is about 137 px wide against a plate about 345 px wide, which gives about 9.5 cm. That seems a little large, so I use a pear width of about 8 cm and a length of about 9 cm.

STEP 3 - Items: One green pear, with no other food.

STEP 4 - Area: The pear covers about 8 × 9 × 0.785 ≈ 57 cm², roughly 10% of the plate. Food covers about 10% of the plate in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: A pear that is 8 cm wide and 9 cm tall is roughly an ellipsoid. Volume = 4/3 × π × 4 × 4 × 4.5 ≈ 300 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit has a density of about 0.6 once the core and air pockets are allowed for, though a pear is close to 0.95 in reality. Using about 0.65 gives roughly 195 g. A typical pear of this size weighs about 180 g, so I take 185 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Pear has about 57 kcal per 100 g. 185 g × 0.57 ≈ 105 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium pear weighing about 185 g and giving about 105 kcal is plausible.
